## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A Táng-period hagiography of Śākyamuni in one juan, compiled by the great vinaya master [道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3) (Dàoxuān, 596–667) and dated by his preface to 665 (Líndé 麟德 2). It supersedes [僧祐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E7%A5%90)'s earlier and longer *Shìjiā pǔ* ([KR6r0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0025)) as a more compact and topically organised handbook, drawing on a wider range of canonical sources, especially those translated by [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) in the years 645–664 (i.e. between [僧祐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E7%A5%90)'s lifetime and [道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3)'s).

**Abstract**

[道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3) composed the *Shìjiā shì pǔ* alongside his much larger and complementary *Shìjiā fāngzhì* 釋迦方志 ([KR6r0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0058)), a geographical compendium on the Buddhist holy land. Where the *Fāngzhì* covers the geography, the *Shì pǔ* covers the genealogy, life, and chief events of the Buddha. The single-juan format was deliberately compact, intended as a handbook for monastics needing quick reference to the canonical narrative.

The structure is topical: ancestry of the Śākya clan; the descent from Tuṣita Heaven; the birth at Lumbinī; the youth and the four signs; the renunciation; the enlightenment; the first sermon; the major life events (return to Kapilavastu, the Devadatta schism, etc.); and the *parinirvāṇa*. Each topic synthesises material from the relevant Indian biographical sūtras (the *Buddhacarita*, *Lalitavistara*, *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya*, etc., supplemented by the new translations of Xuánzàng).

The 665 dating is given in [道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3)'s own preface and is secure. The work was widely used in Táng monastic education and continued as a standard reference into the Sòng.
